article_title: Self-regulated learning and reflection: a tool for teachers and students
citation: Avivit Arvatz, Roee Peretz, Yehudit Judy Dori. (2025). Self-regulated learning and reflection: a tool for teachers and students. Metacognition and Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11409-025-09415-3
title: T-SQsrl: paired teacher and student SRL questionnaires with a triangulated reflection assessment
description: The T-SQsrl is an assessment tool comprising a teacher version (TQsrl, 31 closed-ended items plus an open-ended reflective question) and a student version (SQsrl, 15 closed-ended items), both adapted from the SRLMQ and structured on Zimmerman's cyclical SRL model. It evaluates SRL sub-processes including goal-setting, task-strategy, self-efficacy, help-seeking, elaboration, and reflection. The teacher version enables triangulated assessment by correlating self-assessed reflection with expert grading of an open-ended reflective question, while teachers provided the external assessment triangulating students' self-assessments. The article describes it as innovative in its focus on reflection skills and in allowing simultaneous assessment of teachers' and students' SRL within the same classroom or school.
requirements: External assessment of the reflection skill requires open-ended items graded by experts (for teachers) or by teachers (for students) to triangulate self-reports
constraints: The study notes validity issues with self-reports, and the sampling was a convenience sample with modest sizes adequate for initial validation only
target_learners: students aged 12 and above in grades 7–12
target_learning_goals: assessing SRL sub-processes and reflection skill for formative assessment and intervention design
examples: Ten teachers who participated in the PD administered the SQsrl to their students with parental consent to map baseline SRL before an SRL intervention, and policymakers may use TQsrl results as an indicator of a PD program's effectiveness
key_sources: Avivit Arvatz, Roee Peretz, Yehudit Judy Dori. (2025). Self-regulated learning and reflection: a tool for teachers and students. Metacognition and Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11409-025-09415-3

article_title: Fostering integrated mental models of different professional knowledge domains: instructional approaches and model-based analyses
citation: Lehmann, T., Pirnay-Dummer, P., & Schmidt-Borcherding, F. (2019). Fostering integrated mental models of different professional knowledge domains: instructional approaches and model-based analyses. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09704-0
title: T-MITOCAR as an automated model-based assessment tool for knowledge integration
description: T-MITOCAR (Text-Model Inspection Trace of Concepts and Relations) is an automated computer-based diagnostic tool that uses natural language expressions as input data to generate graph-based representations of learners' mental models. It measures structural and semantic similarities of verbally externalized mental models compared to a reference (expert) model using measures such as GAMMA (structural density) and BSM (balanced semantic matching). The tool relies on "the dependence of syntax and semantics within natural language" and works with a comparably small amount of text (350 words+).
requirements: Requires learners to externalize their mental models in natural language written formulations of at least 350 words
constraints: The reference model configuration may influence results; the authors note their reference model was not an argumentative text
key_sources: Lehmann, T., Pirnay-Dummer, P., & Schmidt-Borcherding, F. (2019). Fostering integrated mental models of different professional knowledge domains: instructional approaches and model-based analyses. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09704-0

article_title: Promoting pre-service teachers’ knowledge integration from multiple text sources across domains with instructional prompts
citation: Inka Sara Hähnlein, Pablo Pirnay-Dummer. (2024). Promoting pre-service teachers' knowledge integration from multiple text sources across domains with instructional prompts. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-024-10363-z
title: T-MITOCAR computer-linguistic technology for modeling and comparing semantic knowledge structures of texts
description: T-MITOCAR (Text-Model Inspection Trace of Concepts and Relations) is a computational linguistic heuristic technology "developed as a means of automatically analyzing, modeling, visualizing, and comparing the semantic knowledge structure of texts." It builds graphs of concepts linked by association strengths from propositional relations, grounded in mental model theory, and compares texts quantitatively via four structural measures (SUR, GRA, GAMMA, STRU) and three semantic measures (CONC, PROP, BSM) yielding similarity values between zero and one. The study used it to compare student texts with a reference model of the four source texts.
requirements: A reference model built from the source texts against which learner texts are compared using the seven similarity measures
constraints: The article states the similarity indices measure different features and "can therefore not be treated like a subsuming scale (e.g., on a test)"
target_learning_goals: assessing semantic knowledge structure of learner-produced texts
examples: The four source texts were combined into one document and modelled with T-MITOCAR to generate the reference model against which all 109 student texts were compared
key_sources: Inka Sara Hähnlein, Pablo Pirnay-Dummer. (2024). Promoting pre-service teachers' knowledge integration from multiple text sources across domains with instructional prompts. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-024-10363-z
